about: The code examples of the chapter 5 deck, in the order of the code slides (order = slide order). The page's chapter-code tab lists them by NAME in this order; the code runs in the page with the chapter library and the prelude defined first; the expected result is what the run printed.

page_requirements: hashlib with sha256, sha512, pbkdf2_hmac and ripemd160
wordlist() reads the BIP39 English word list (2048 words) from the data file

prelude:
import json
sha256_hex = lambda b: hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
ENT = "0c1e24e5917779d297e14d45f14e1a1a"
WORDS = "army van defense carry jealous true garbage claim echo media make crunch"
PASSPHRASE = "SuperDuperSecret"
TV = bytes.fromhex("000102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f")
B84 = "abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon abandon about"
DESC = ("wpkh([73c5da0a/84h/0h/0h]xpub6CatWdiZiodmUeTDp8LT5or8nmbKNcuyvz7WyksVFkKB4RHwCD3Xyuv"
        "PEbvqAQY3rAPshWcMLoP2fMFMKHPJ4ZeZXYVUhLv1VMrjPC7PW6V/0/*)")

examples.name: Loose keys versus one seed
examples.code:
seed = b"my seed"
key = lambda i: sha256_hex(seed + bytes([i]))
keys = [key(i)[:8] for i in range(3)]
print(keys)
again = [key(i)[:8] for i in range(3)]
print(keys == again)

examples.name: Other recovery codes check themselves differently
examples.code:
print(codex32_check(C32))
n = next(i for i in range(99999)
         if electrum_has_version("seed %d" % i, "100"))
print(n, electrum_hash("seed %d" % n)[:3])

examples.name: Three of five shares recover the secret
examples.code:
secret = 0x1337c0de
shares = shamir_split(secret, 3, 5, [11, 22])
print(shamir_combine(shares[:3]) == secret)
print(shamir_combine(shares[1:4]) == secret)
print(shamir_combine(shares[:2]) == secret)

examples.name: A hash function changes half its bits
examples.code:
a = hashlib.sha256(b"seed A").digest()
b = hashlib.sha256(b"seed B").digest()
diff = int(a.hex(), 16) ^ int(b.hex(), 16)
print(len(a) * 8, bin(diff).count("1"))

examples.name: How many words for how much entropy
examples.code:
for bits in (128, 160, 192, 224, 256):
    ent = bytes(bits // 8)
    n = len(entropy_to_mnemonic(ent).split())
    print(bits, n)

examples.name: From entropy to twelve words
examples.code:
words = entropy_to_mnemonic(bytes.fromhex(ENT))
print(words == WORDS)
idx = [wordlist().index(w) for w in words.split()]
print(idx)
print(format(idx[0], "011b"), words.split()[0])

examples.name: The checksum catches a wrong word
examples.code:
ent, ok = mnemonic_to_entropy(WORDS)
print(ent.hex(), ok)
bad = WORDS.replace("crunch", "army")
print(mnemonic_to_entropy(bad)[1])

examples.name: Text is normalised before stretching
examples.code:
s = "caf\u00e9"
n = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", s)
print(len(s), len(n))
print(mnemonic_to_seed(s) == mnemonic_to_seed(n))

examples.name: PBKDF2 stretches the words with a salt
examples.code:
def stretch(salt, rounds):
    d = hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac(
        "sha512", WORDS.encode(), salt, rounds)
    return d.hex()[:12]
print(stretch(b"mnemonic", 1))
print(stretch(b"mnemonic", 2048))
print(stretch(b"mnemonic1", 2048))

examples.name: A passphrase opens a different wallet
HMAC-SHA512 makes the master key
examples.code:
h = hmac.new(b"Bitcoin seed", TV, hashlib.sha512)
I = h.digest()
left, right = I[:32], I[32:]
print(len(I), len(left), len(right))
k, c = master(TV)
print(k == int.from_bytes(left, "big"), c == right)
print("%064x" % k)

examples.name: Child keys from a parent and an index
examples.code:
k, c = master(TV)
for i in range(3):
    ki, ci = ckd_priv(k, c, i)
    print(i, "%064x" % ki, ci.hex())

examples.name: Hardened and normal children differ
concepts: index numbers for normal and hardened derivation
examples.code:
k, c = master(TV)
normal, _ = ckd_priv(k, c, 0)
hard, _ = ckd_priv(k, c, HARD)
print(HARD, normal == hard)
print(path_indices("m/0h") == [HARD])

examples.name: Why hardened steps protect the parent
examples.code:
k, c = master(TV)
K = ec_mul(k)
kid, _ = ckd_priv(k, c, 5)
back = leak_parent_private_key(K, c, 5, kid)
print(back == k)

examples.name: Public keys derived without private keys
examples.code:
k, c = master(TV)
K = ec_mul(k)
k5, _ = ckd_priv(k, c, 5)
K5, _ = ckd_pub(K, c, 5)
print(ec_mul(k5) == K5)

examples.name: Extended keys: xprv, xpub and a fingerprint
examples.code:
k, c = master(TV)
xprv = serialize_xprv(k, c)
xpub = serialize_xpub(ec_mul(k), c)
print(xprv[:4], len(xprv), xpub[:4], len(xpub))
print(fingerprint(ec_mul(k)).hex())
print(parse_extended(xpub)["depth"])

examples.name: 2 to the 31 children, normal and hardened
examples.code:
print(2**31, HARD, 2**31 - 1)
print(len(range(0, HARD)), len(range(HARD, 2 * HARD)))

examples.name: Reading a key path level by level
examples.code:
path = "m/84h/0h/0h/1/7"
idx = path_indices(path)
names = "purpose coin account change index".split()
for n, i in zip(names, idx):
    print(n, i, i >= HARD)
examples.expected:
purpose 2147483732 True
coin 2147483648 True
account 2147483648 True
change 1 False
index 7 False

examples.name: Four standard paths, four address types
examples.code:
pub = lambda p: ser_p(ec_mul(keys_at(B84, p)[0]))
a44 = p2pkh(pub("m/44h/0h/0h/0/0"))
s = b"\x00\x14" + hash160(pub("m/49h/0h/0h/0/0"))
a49 = b58check(b"\x05" + hash160(s))
a84 = p2wpkh_address(pub("m/84h/0h/0h/0/0"))
q = taproot_output_key(pub("m/86h/0h/0h/0/0"))
a86 = p2tr_address(q)
print(a44, a49, a84, a86, sep="\n")

examples.name: Our address equals the standard's own
examples.code:
k, c = keys_at(B84, "m/84h/0h/0h/0/0")
addr = p2wpkh_address(ser_p(ec_mul(k)))
published = "bc1qcr8te4kr609gcawutmrza0j4xv80jy8z306fyu"
print(addr == published)

examples.name: A key tweak makes the taproot key
examples.code:
k, c = keys_at(B84, "m/86h/0h/0h/0/0")
P = ser_p(ec_mul(k))
Q = taproot_output_key(P)
print(P[1:].hex()[:12], Q.hex()[:12])
print(p2tr_address(Q))

examples.name: A descriptor with its checksum and key origin
examples.code:

fp, steps = parse_origin(DESC)
print(fp, [s >= HARD for s in steps])
multi = "wsh(multi(2,A,B,C))"
print(descsum_create(multi))

examples.name: Labels exported in the BIP329 format
examples.code:

rows = [dict(type="addr", ref=a, label="rent"),

examples.name: A web shop that holds no private key
examples.code:
acct = parse_extended(BOOK_XPUB)
K = decompress(acct["key"])
for i in range(3):
    Ki, _ = ckd_pub(K, acct["chain"], i)
    print(i, p2wpkh_address(ser_p(Ki)))

examples.name: The gap limit decides how far a scan looks
A digital signature fails if the message changes
examples.code:
d = 0x1337
pub = ec_mul(d)
z = int(sha256_hex(b"pay 1"), 16)
sig = ecdsa_sign(d, z, 4242)
z2 = int(sha256_hex(b"pay 2"), 16)
print(ecdsa_verify(pub, z, sig))
print(ecdsa_verify(pub, z2, sig))
